Who We Are

Our coffee export business is directly connected with local coffee farmers, which means we know exactly where our exportable green beans come from. This ensures our buyers receive genuine single-origin coffee with full transparency.  Our beans are stored in our own clean and secure warehouse, ensuring consistency and freshness. That’s why our samples truly represent the quality of our actual coffee products.we pride ourselves on being a trusted partner for roasters, importers, and investors.

Discover Our Premium
Ethiopian Coffee Selection

We offer a curated selection of single-origin beans, organic options, and specialty blends from Ethiopia’s renowned coffee-growing regions.

The Grade Scale

  • Grade 1: 91-100 points. The highest quality, with very few physical defects (under 5). 
  • Grade 2: 81-90 points. A very high-quality coffee with a slight increase in defects (5-12). 
  • Grade 3: 71-80 points. The lowest grade often considered specialty, with 13-25 defects in natural coffees. 
  • Grade 4: 63-70 points. A standard-grade coffee with 26-46 defects. 
  • Grade 5: These are lower commercial grades with increasing numbers of physical defects. 

Sidamo Coffee

Origin: Sidamo, Southern Ethiopia
Altitude: 1,600 – 2,000 meters
Processing Method: Washed or Natural

Description:
Sidamo Coffee offers a balanced cup with hints of berries, chocolate, and citrus. It’s versatile enough for espresso, drip, or French press, making it a favorite among roasters and cafés around the world.

Flavor Profile

AttributeDescription
AromaSweet and fruity
BodyMedium and smooth
AcidityGentle and balanced
AftertasteClean and lingering
Flavor NotesBerries, cocoa, and citrus

Brewing Recommendations

Best Brewing Methods: French Press, Drip, Espresso
Recommended Ratio: 1:16 (coffee to water)
Brew Time: 4–5 minutes

Sustainability & Sourcing

Our Sidamo beans are handpicked from smallholder farms, promoting sustainable agriculture and community growth. Every cup supports local farmers and preserves Ethiopia’s coffee legacy.

Yirgacheffe Coffee

Origin: Yirgacheffe, Southern Ethiopia
Altitude: 1,700 – 2,200 meters
Processing Method: Washed (Wet Process)

Description:
Yirgacheffe Coffee is Ethiopia’s most celebrated variety, known for its delicate floral notes, lemon zest brightness, and smooth body. Ideal for both espresso and pour-over, it’s loved by specialty roasters and coffee enthusiasts across the globe.

Flavor Profile

AttributeDescription
AromaFloral and citrusy
BodyLight and silky
AcidityBright and clean
AftertasteSweet and refreshing
Flavor NotesJasmine, lemon, and honey

Brewing Recommendations

Best Brewing Methods: Pour-over, Chemex, Cold Brew
Recommended Ratio: 1:15 (coffee to water)
Brew Time: 3–4 minutes

Sustainability & Sourcing

Our Yirgacheffe beans are ethically sourced directly from smallholder farmers, ensuring fair compensation and eco-friendly practices. Every bag you buy supports local Ethiopian farming communities and sustainable coffee production.

Harrar Coffee

Origin: Harrar, Eastern Ethiopia
Altitude: 1,400 – 2,000 meters
Processing Method: Natural (Dry Process)

Description:
Harrar Coffee delivers a rich, winey cup with notes of dark chocolate, blueberry, and spice. Perfect for strong coffee lovers who prefer an intense aroma and depth in flavor.

Flavor Profile

AttributeDescription
AromaIntense and spicy
BodyFull and heavy
AcidityMild but vibrant
AftertasteDeep and lingering
Flavor NotesBlueberry, dark chocolate, spice

Brewing Recommendations

Best Brewing Methods: Espresso, Moka Pot, Cold Brew
Recommended Ratio: 1:14 (coffee to water)
Brew Time: 3–4 minutes

Sustainability & Sourcing

Our Harrar beans are sourced from traditional dry-processing farms, where sun-drying and hand-sorting maintain Ethiopia’s authentic flavor and heritage.

Limu Coffee

Origin: Limu, Western Ethiopia
Altitude: 1,400 – 1,900 meters
Processing Method: Washed

Description:
Limu Coffee offers a smooth, clean cup with delicate citrus and caramel notes. Its naturally sweet taste and medium body make it ideal for both pour-over and drip brews.

Flavor Profile

AttributeDescription
AromaSweet and floral
BodyMedium and clean
AcidityMild and balanced
AftertasteSoft and smooth
Flavor NotesCitrus, caramel, and honey

Brewing Recommendations

Best Brewing Methods: Pour-over, Drip, Aeropress
Recommended Ratio: 1:15 (coffee to water)
Brew Time: 3–4 minutes

Sustainability & Sourcing

Limu Coffee farmers practice shade-grown, eco-friendly cultivation, preserving the natural forest environment and supporting biodiversity in Western Ethiopia.

Arsi Coffee

Origin: Arsi, Southeastern Ethiopia
Altitude: 1,600 – 2,200 meters
Processing Method: Washed & Natural

Description:
Arsi Coffee delivers a bright, lively cup with floral and sweet citrus characteristics. Known for its clean profile and smooth mouthfeel, this coffee shines in filter brews and iced methods.

Flavor Profile

AttributeDescription

BodyLight to medium
AcidityBright and crisp
AftertasteFresh and delicate

Brewing Recommendations

Brew Time: 3–4 minutes

Sustainability & Sourcing

Arsi farmers cultivate coffee with traditional shade-grown methods, using natural compost and eco-friendly practices that preserve local forests and wildlife.

Guji Coffee

Origin: Guji, Oromia Region
Altitude: 1,800 – 2,300 meters
Processing Method: Natural & Washed

Description:
Guji Coffee is highly prized for its unique sweetness and fruity complexity. A vibrant cup with silky texture and berry-forward notes, perfect for specialty coffee drinkers.

Sustainability & Sourcing

Guji farmers follow organic-forward farming, hand-picking cherries and practicing forest conservation through agro-forestry systems.

posts.title: Why Ethiopian Coffee is the World’s Favorite
posts.html:
Ethiopian coffee holds a legendary status among coffee lovers, roasters, and investors worldwide. As the birthplace of coffee, Ethiopia’s beans are prized for their unmatched flavors, rich cultural heritage, and sustainable farming traditions. But what makes Ethiopian coffee the world’s favorite? Let’s dive in.

1. The Birthplace of Coffee

Ethiopia is globally recognized as the origin of Arabica coffee. Every cup connects you to centuries of tradition, culture, and craftsmanship that started in Ethiopia’s highlands.

2. Unique Flavor Profiles

  • Yirgacheffe: Bright acidity, floral, and citrus notes.

  • Sidamo: Smooth, fruity, and full-bodied.

  • Harrar: Bold, earthy, and berry-like flavors.
    Ethiopian beans offer diversity unmatched by any other region.

3. Sustainability at the Core

Most Ethiopian coffee is naturally grown, hand-picked, and sun-dried, ensuring environmentally friendly production while preserving authentic taste.

4. Preferred by Global Roasters

From specialty cafés in Europe to large-scale roasters in Asia, Ethiopian coffee remains the first choice for those seeking consistency, quality, and flavor innovation.

Conclusion
Whether you’re a coffee enthusiast, roaster, or importer, Ethiopian coffee continues to dominate the global market for good reason — it’s more than a drink; it’s an experience.

posts.title: Investing in the Future of Ethiopian Coffee
posts.html:
Ethiopian coffee is not only world-renowned for quality but also a strong and growing investment sector. With global demand for specialty coffee rising, Ethiopia offers exciting opportunities for investors, exporters, and distributors.

1. Growing Global Demand

The specialty coffee market is booming, and Ethiopian beans are at the center of this growth. Consumers are willing to pay premium prices for authentic, traceable, and organic coffee.

2. Opportunities for Investors

  • Direct sourcing and exports

  • Processing and roasting facilities

  • Partnerships with cooperatives and local farmers

  • Sustainable farming and organic certifications

3. Government Support and Trade Expansion

Ethiopia’s government actively promotes coffee exports, improving logistics, regulations, and international trade agreements.

4. Sustainable and Ethical Investments

Investors can take part in projects that ensure fair wages, eco-friendly practices, and long-term growth — appealing to socially conscious buyers.

Conclusion
Investing in Ethiopian coffee is more than profit — it’s contributing to a sustainable, global movement while tapping into one of the fastest-growing sectors in agriculture.

posts.title: Ethiopian Coffee Export Regulations: What You Need to Know
posts.html:
Exporting Ethiopian coffee requires navigating specific regulations and standards. For roasters, importers, and investors, understanding these rules is key to smooth operations and successful business partnerships.

1. Licensing Requirements

Coffee exporters in Ethiopia must hold a valid export license issued by the Ethiopian Coffee & Tea Authority.

2. Quality Control Standards

All Ethiopian coffee passes through strict quality checks, grading systems, and certifications to meet international requirements.

3. Traceability and Documentation

Exporters must provide:

  • Certificates of Origin

  • Phytosanitary Certificates

  • Coffee Quality Certificates

  • Customs declarations

4. Logistics and Shipping

Addis Ababa serves as the main hub for coffee exports, with shipments processed through the Djibouti port for international trade.

Conclusion
By understanding Ethiopia’s export regulations, roasters and investors can ensure compliance, avoid delays, and strengthen partnerships with reliable Ethiopian exporters.

posts.title: Ethiopian Coffee Gains Strength in Global Markets
posts.html:
Ethiopian Coffee Gains Strength in Global Markets

Ethiopian coffee continues to capture attention across the global commodities market. According to the latest data, coffee is currently trading at $368.46 USD, showing a 0.17% daily increase. This small yet consistent growth highlights the steady demand for premium Arabica beans — especially from regions like Yirgacheffe, Sidamo, and Harrar.

Coffee opened today at $368.55 with a maximum of $372.98 and a minimum of $361.13, signaling strong buyer interest and stable performance amid global market fluctuations.

Why the World Watches Ethiopian Coffee

Ethiopia’s unique coffee origin is not just about taste — it’s about legacy and sustainability. Every bean grown in the highlands tells a story of tradition, quality, and craftsmanship. As global buyers seek traceable and ethically sourced coffee, Ethiopian exports continue to gain a competitive edge.

With increasing international demand and growing local investment, the coffee sector is becoming one of Ethiopia’s strongest economic drivers — attracting roasters, exporters, and investors from all over the world.

Market Insights for Investors

For investors, the current trading stability presents a promising window of opportunity. Ethiopia’s coffee industry benefits from:

  • Strong global recognition of its flavor profile

  • Rising export volumes year after year

  • Expanding specialty coffee markets in Europe, the U.S., and Asia

Keeping an eye on the live coffee price helps both exporters and investors make informed trading and purchasing decisions.

Sustainability and the Future of Coffee Trade

With ongoing initiatives in sustainable farming and fair trade practices, Ethiopian coffee producers are positioning themselves for long-term growth. The balance between preserving traditional methods and meeting modern demand is what keeps the Ethiopian coffee story powerful — and profitable.

posts.title: 2025/2026 Production Will Be Ready Mid-December for Export Market
posts.html:
2025/2026 Production Will Be Ready Mid-December for Export Market

We are pleased to announce that our 2025/2026 coffee production season is progressing exceptionally well, with harvest and processing phases currently underway across our partner farms in Ethiopia’s renowned coffee-growing regions. According to our production timeline, export-ready coffee will be available by mid-December, aligning perfectly with global trading schedules and roasters’ procurement cycles.

This season promises enhanced quality, thanks to improved farm-level practices, strict harvesting standards, and advanced post-harvest processing techniques. Farmers have adopted selective hand-picking, eco-friendly washing systems, and optimized drying protocols to ensure consistency in cup profile, moisture level, and bean structure.

What to Expect This Season

  • Premium-grade specialty and commercial lots
  • Strict traceability from farm to export
  • Washed, natural, and honey-processed varieties
  • Flexible export packaging options (60kg & customized bulk options)
  • Pre-shipment quality inspection and cupping profiles

With global demand steadily rising for authentic Ethiopian coffee, our preparation ensures timely delivery, superior bean quality, and stable supply capacity for international buyers, roasters, and distributors.

We invite buyers to begin placing advance orders and sample requests. Early reservation ensures access to top-lot selections and priority scheduling for shipment once this season’s coffees are fully conditioned and certified for export.

For inquiries, forward booking, and cupping samples, please contact us — we look forward to partnering with you for a successful 2025/2026 coffee export season.
